Weyl integral (named after [Hermann Weyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Weyl)) is an operator defined, as an example of [fractional calculus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fractional_calculus), on functions f on the [unit circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_circle) having integral 0 and a [Fourier series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourier_series).
Weyl's law describes the asymptotic behavior of eigenvalues of the [Laplace–Beltrami operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laplace–Beltrami_operator).

Weyl's lemma, named after [Hermann Weyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Weyl), states that every [weak solution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weak_solution) of [Laplace's equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laplace's_equation) is a [smooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_function) solution.

white noise analysis, otherwise known as Hida calculus, is a framework for infinite-dimensional and [stochastic calculus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic_calculus), based on the [Gaussian white noise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaussian_white_noise) [probability space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probability_space), to be compared with [Malliavin calculus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malliavin_calculus) based on the [Wiener process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiener_process).

Whitham equation is a non-local model for [non-linear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-linear_system) [dispersive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dispersion_relation) [wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave)s.

Wiener's lemma is a well-known identity which relates the asymptotic behaviour of the Fourier coefficients of a [Borel measure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borel_measure) on the [circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle_group) to its discrete part.
Wiener–Hopf method is a mathematical technique widely used in [applied mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applied_mathematics).
Wirtinger inequality is an important inequality for functions of a single variable, named after [Wilhelm Wirtinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelm_Wirtinger).

definition: Workshop on Numerical Ranges and Numerical Radii (WONRA) is a biennial workshop series on [numerical range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Numerical_range)s and numerical radii which began in 1992.
Ximera (pronounced “chimera”) is an open-source, interactive textbook platform, most commonly used in teaching math.

Yamada–Watanabe theorem is a result from [probability theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probability_theory) saying that for a large class of [stochastic differential equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic_differential_equation)s a weak solution with pathwise uniqueness implies a strong solution and uniqueness in distribution.

Yang–Mills–Higgs equations are a set of [non-linear partial differential equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-linear_partial_differential_equation)s for a [Yang–Mills field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yang–Mills_field), given by a connection, and a [Higgs field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higgs_field), given by a section of a [vector bundle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_bundle) (specifically, the [adjoint bundle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adjoint_bundle)).

Young–Laplace equation () is an equation that describes the [capillary pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capillary_pressure) difference sustained across the interface between two [static fluids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluid_statics), such as [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water) and [air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air), due to the phenomenon of [surface tension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surface_tension) or [wall tension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_tension) acting against the curvature of the surface (although use of the latter is only applicable if assuming that the wall is very thin).
Zakai equation is a linear [stochastic partial differential equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic_partial_differential_equation) for the un-normalized density of a hidden state.
Zakharov system is a system of non-linear partial differential equations, introduced by [[Vladimir E.

Zakharov–Schulman system is a system of nonlinear [partial differential equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial_differential_equation)s introduced in to describe the interactions of small amplitude, high frequency waves with [acoustic wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoustic_wave)s.

Zeldovich–Taylor flow (also known as Zeldovich–Taylor expansion wave) is the fluid motion of gaseous detonation products behind [Chapman–Jouguet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapman–Jouguet_condition) [detonation wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detonation_wave).

zero dynamics describes the internal behavior of a dynamic system when its outputs are constrained to [zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero) through control inputs (e.g., maintaining a robot arm at a fixed position while internal states continue to evolve).

definition: zeta function regularization is a type of [regularization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regularization_(physics)) or [summability method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summability_method) that assigns finite values to [divergent sums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divergent_series) or products, and in particular can be used to define [determinant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinant)s and [trace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trace_(linear_algebra))s of some [self-adjoint operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-adjoint_operator)s.

ZFK equation, abbreviation for Zeldovich–Frank-Kamenetskii equation, is a [reaction–diffusion equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reaction–diffusion_system) that models [premixed flame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premixed_flame) propagation.

Zubov's method is a technique for computing the [basin of attraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basin_of_attraction) for a set of [ordinary differential equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordinary_differential_equation)s (a [dynamical system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamical_system)).
